newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Phone companies should divest cable - expert.
newsitem.headline: Phone companies should divest cable - expert.

text.p: Phone companies such as Deutsche Telekom should be asked to divest their cable television operations to ensure telecommunications markets are fully competitive, a telecoms experts said on Monday.
"I think they should (divest) if your objective is competition," Graham Finnie, director of British-based telecoms consultancy Yankee Group Europe, told reporters attending a telecoms seminar.

As part of its effort to liberalise European Union telecoms markets, the European Commission is studying whether to take action against dominant phone companies such as Deutsche Telekom and to a lesser extent France Telecom that operate cable networks.
It is expecting an independent study on the question later this month from consultants Arthur D. Little.

Finnie said cable companies should be independent because they were well-placed to compete with dominant operators in the "local" segment of telecoms networks -- the connection between houses and telephone switches -- and thus help bring prices of local calls down.
He cited the British market, where all cable operators also provide telephone service.
